metadata.title: Noah Fant - Cleared to play vs. Minnesota
metadata.description: Fant (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Fant opened the week with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag and return from a one-game absence due to an abdominal injury. He has an 8-66-3 receiving line (on 12 targets) through three regular-season games while operating as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Fant (abdomen) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: After sitting out Monday's loss to Atlanta, Fant has had his reps capped for the Saints' first two Week 5 practices while he continues to manage the abdominal injury. He'll likely need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid taking a designation into Sunday's matchup with the Vikings. When available this season, Fant has been productive as the Saints' No. 2 tight end behind Juwan Johnson, registering eight receptions for 66 yards and three touchdowns on 12 targets over three appearances.

metadata.title: Noah Fant (abdomen) limited participant Thursday
metadata.description: Noah Fant (abdomen) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Fant was limited for another practice on Thursday as he continues to recover from an injury to his abdomen. He seems to be trending towards playing in Week 5, but we won't know his status for sure until after practice on Friday.

metadata.title: Noah Fant (abdomen) limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Noah Fant (abdomen) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The Saints were without Fant in Week 4, as he was sidelined due to the same abdomen issue that left him limited at practice on Wednesday. He seems to be trending towards playing in Week 5, but we won't get official word until later on in the week.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Fant (abdomen) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Fant missed Monday night's loss to the Falcons, but his limited start to the week would seem to give the veteran tight end a good shot to return to the field for Week 5 against the Vikings. He's turned 12 targets into eight catches for 66 yards and three touchdowns this season as one of Tyler Shough's favorite targets near the end zone.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Inactive in Week 4
metadata.description: Fant (abdomen) is listed as inactive for Monday's game against the Falcons.
metadata.analysis: Despite being a limited practice participant during Week 4 prep, Fant will miss his first contest of the campaign due to an abdominal injury. Oscar Delp and Treyton Welch thus will serve as the reserve tight ends behind starter Juwan Johnson on Monday. Fant's next chance to play is this coming Sunday versus the Vikings.

metadata.title: Noah Fant Inactive on Monday Night With Abdominal Injury
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints tight end Noah Fant (abdomen) is officially inactive for the Monday night game against the division-rival Atlanta Falcons to close out Week 4 action, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football. The 28-year-old was limited in practice Thursday through Saturday, but it was not enough to convince the coaching staff that he was ready to play against the Falcons. Fant scored a touchdown in the season opener and caught all four of his targets for 33 yards and two more touchdowns in last week's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. However, in three games played going into Monday's contest, he has only eight receptions on 12 targets for 66 yards through the air as the clear No. 2 tight end in New Orleans behind Juwan Johnson, who has been a target hog in the early going in the Saints' offense. With Fant sidelined on Monday, Oscar Delp and Treyton Welch will battle for scraps at the position behind Johnson. At best, Fant is a touchdown-dependent TE2 for fantasy managers in deeper leagues when he is healthy.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Questionable for MNF
metadata.description: Fant (abdomen) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Falcons, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
metadata.analysis: Fant's practice participation was limited all week due to an abdominal injury that he likely picked up in Week 3 against the Raiders. With the questionable tag, the veteran tight end's status for Monday may not be known until the Saints announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. Oscar Delp and Treyton Welch would see more rotational snaps at tight end behind Juwan Johnson if Fant is not cleared to play against Atlanta.

metadata.title: Noah Fant Questionable to Face Falcons in Week 4
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints tight end Noah Fant (abdomen) is officially listed as questionable to play in Monday's Week 4 contest against the Atlanta Falcons, according to Jeff Nowak of Audacy Sports. Fant was limited in practice all week long, so it appears that he could be a true game-time decision for Monday Night Football. We don't expect his status to impact too many fantasy managers, as Fant is currently rostered in just 2% of leagues. With that being said, his availability could be crucial for the Saints, given that he has scored three touchdowns through three games. Last week, he caught four passes for 33 yards with two trips to the end zone. He currently ranks #14 among tight ends in fantasy scoring this season, but Juwan Johnson (TE4 overall) remains the only Saints tight end worth starting, regardless of whether Fant suits up.

metadata.title: Noah Fant Limited Again on Friday
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints tight end Noah Fant (abdomen) was a limited participant in Friday's practice as the team gears up for a Monday night home matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. That's two limited sessions to start the week for Fant, who has already scored three touchdowns in 2026. While it's unlikely he's been active on many fantasy rosters, the former first-round pick is the current TE14 in PPR formats. Whether that is sustainable remains to be seen, but Fant plays a decent amount of snaps on a high-powered, fast-paced offense and offers some appeal in deep leagues and best ball formats. If the 28-year-old is unable to suit up for Monday's contest, Treyton Welch and Oscar Delp figure to help fill the void behind Juwan Johnson in the Saints' attack.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Another limited session
metadata.description: Fant (abdomen) practiced in a limited capacity Friday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
metadata.analysis: Fant maintained his activity level for a second session in a row, giving him just one more chance to get back to full this week. Saturday's injury report will reveal if he's in danger of missing Monday's game against the Falcons due to his abdominal issue.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Dealing with abdominal issue
metadata.description: Fant was limited in practice Thursday due to an abdominal injury.
metadata.analysis: Fant has taken full advantage of his 12 targets through three games this season, turning them into eight catches for 66 yards and three touchdowns. Now, a health concern is impacting him at the start of Week 4 prep, so his status bears watching as the Saints ramp up for Monday's matchup with the Falcons.

metadata.title: Noah Fant hauls in two touchdowns Sunday
metadata.description: Noah Fant caught 4-of-4 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Fant and Juwan Johnson both hauled in two touchdowns on the day. Despite that, Fant remains off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Two touchdowns in loss
metadata.description: Fant caught all four of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 35-27 loss to Las Vegas.
metadata.analysis: Fant made the most of his opportunities, connecting with quarterback Tyler Shough for a three-yard touchdown in the second quarter and a 16-yard score in the third quarter. The tight end is the No. 2 option behind Juwan Johnson at his position, but Fant has still caught eight of 12 targets for 66 yards and three scores over the first three games this year.

metadata.title: Noah Fant Could Have Deep-League Appeal
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints tight end Noah Fant recorded four receptions on eight targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in Week 1's loss to the Detroit Lions. Fant was on the field for 41% of the Saints' offensive snaps, but showed good chemistry with second-year quarterback Tyler Shough, reeling in an eight-yard touchdown grab at the end of overtime to give New Orleans a chance to win the game. Shough connected with Fant and fellow tight end Juwan Johnson for a combined 87 yards and two touchdowns on 15 targets. If Shough continues to target his tight ends at a high rate, Fant could develop some standalone appeal in deeper leagues. With his limited snap share, there are still some concerns, but Fant is worth keeping an eye on or stashing for the time being.

metadata.title: Noah Fant Building Momentum Heading into Week 2
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints tight end Noah Fant was targeted eight times in Week 1 and caught four passes for 33 yards and a touchdown. The Saints fell to the Detroit Lions 31-30 in overtime, but quarterback Tyler Shough put up 410 passing yards and showed he will spread the ball around. Fellow tight end Juwan Johnson recorded three receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, proving further that Shough has no issue targeting tight ends. The Saints have a Week 2 game against the Baltimore Ravens, and while it is likely going to be a tougher matchup for Fant, he could be worth a roster spot for fantasy teams in need of better tight end play. Fant is available in every league, as he is currently rostered in 0% of Yahoo leagues.

metadata.title: Noah Fant catches touchdown in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Noah Fant caught four of his eight targets for 33 yards and one touchdown in the Saints' 31-30 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Fant saw plenty of involvement in the New Orleans offense, finishing third on the team in targets and receptions in the loss. The tight end will need to offer more impactful output to be trusted, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Scores in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Fant caught four of his eight targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions.
metadata.analysis: Tyler Shough enjoyed targeting tight ends in Sunday's shootout, with the duo of Fant and Juwan Johnson totalling 87 yards and two touchdowns between them. If Shough's favoritism for the bigger-bodied targets with a higher catch radius continues, Fant could become a solid option in deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Noah Fant Unlikely to See a Fantasy Revival in New Orleans
metadata.description: A first-round pick of the Denver Broncos in 2019, tight end Noah Fant has never quite lived up to the hype with which he entered the league, and the latest chapter in his eight-year career saw him sign a two-year, $8.8 million deal with the New Orleans Saints at the start of 2026 free agency. Playing in 15 games for the Bengals in 2025, Fant caught 34 passes for a career-low 288 yards, and in New Orleans, he's now part of a deep tight end room that could make it difficult for him to see much more than a complementary role. Veteran Juwan Johnson was one of only eight tight ends to see triple-digit targets in 2025, and the Saints spent a third-round pick on Georgia's Oscar Delp in the 2026 NFL Draft. While New Orleans should again have one of the most high-volume passing attacks under head coach Kellen Moore, there are a growing number of mouths to feed, with eighth overall pick Jordyn Tyson joining 2025 second-team All-Pro Chris Olave, and running back Travis Etienne Jr. coming aboard as one of the splashier signings of free agency. Buried on the depth chart and not a strong enough blocker to force his way onto the field, Fant is RotoBaller's dynasty TE51 and not a player to expect much from as he enters his age-29 season.

metadata.title: Noah Fant Profiles as a Dynasty Drop Candidate Entering 2026
metadata.description: New Orleans Saints tight end Noah Fant is coming off one of the least productive seasons of his career in 2025, recording 34 receptions for 288 yards and three touchdowns on 41 targets across 15 games for the Cincinnati Bengals. While Fant's production was enough to land him a two-year, $8.75 million contract from the Saints, just $4.5 million of Fant's money is guaranteed. His playing time outlook in New Orleans is also highly uncertain, as Saints TE1 Juwan Johnson is coming off a breakout season and the team used a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft on University of Georgia tight end Oscar Delp. As he enters his eighth year in the NFL, Fant has now failed to record more than 50 catches or 500 receiving yards in a season since 2021. Dynasty managers should feel comfortable dropping Fant as he enters his age-29 campaign.

metadata.title: Noah Fant signs two-year deal with Saints
metadata.description: Veteran tight end Noah Fant and the New Orleans Saints have agreed on a two-year deal.
metadata.analysis: Fant played last season with the Bengals and caught 34 passes for 288 yards and three touchdowns. He has 334 career receptions in his seven-year NFL career with the Broncos, Seahawks, and Bengals with 18 of his catches going for touchdowns. Fant gives the Saints two - sometimes three if you count uber-utility man Taysom Hill - pass catching tight ends for second-year quarterback Tyler Shough. With Johnson enjoying a breakout season last year, Fant will likely be utilized as a backup and in two tight end sets.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Heading to New Orleans
metadata.description: Fant is set to sign a two-year contract with the Saints, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Fant is unlikely to have much fantasy value, joining a team that signed Juwan Johnson to a three-year extension last offseason. Johnson figures to get most of the playing time in passing situations, with Fant more of a factor on early downs and in multi-TE sets. Anything more than 2-to-3 targets per game likely would depend on Johnson missing time.

metadata.title: Saints Agree to Terms With Noah Fant on Two-Year Deal
metadata.description: The New Orleans Saints agreed to terms with free-agent tight end Noah Fant on an undisclosed two-year deal, sources told Tom Pelissero of the NFL Network. Fant will give the Saints some additional tight end depth behind Juwan Johnson, with both Foster Moreau and Taysom Hill (knee) being free agents. The 28-year-old former first-round pick by the Denver Broncos in 2019 out of Iowa had a career-low 288 yards and three touchdowns on 34 receptions (41 targets) in 15 games (seven starts) in his lone season with the Cincinnati Bengals last year. Before that, Fant spent three years with the Seattle Seahawks, never topping 500 receiving yards or four touchdowns in his time there. His career-high of 673 receiving yards came in 2020 with Denver in his second year in the league. Unless Johnson misses time with an injury in 2026, Fant won't be a target in standard-sized 12-team fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Noah Fant - Another lost fumble
metadata.description: Fant caught one pass for five yards in Sunday's loss to the Browns, but he coughed up that reception, and that fumble was returned for a touchdown for the third time this season.
metadata.analysis: Fant's fumble was the perfect cap to a truly disappointing season, one where he caught 34 passes for 288 yards and three touchdowns. The last of those scores came Week 9 against the Bears. He enters the offseason as a free agent after signing a one-year, $2.75 million deal with the Bengals in July.
